items.title: all2html
items.text:
all2html turns design documents into responsive web output. It started as a clean-room ai2html-style exporter for Illustrator and now includes After Effects, Figma, and SVG import paths that all meet at the same canonical IR and rendering pipeline.

This project is pre-launch right now. Try everything. Some paths are more polished than others, but the point of this site is to make the current options understandable, downloadable, and easy to test.

  • Download Illustrator script
  • Download panel .zxp
  • Install .zxp with ZXPInstaller
  • Download After Effects script
  • Download Figma plugin
  • Open the SVG browser converter
  • Install all2html
  • Browse export demos
  • Learn how it works
  • Open the latest GitHub release

Direct download: all2html-figma-plugin.zip

items.title: Build From Source
items.text:
If you want every surface available locally:

pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm build:illustrator
pnpm build:panel
pnpm package:after-effects
pnpm build:figma
pnpm build:svg-dropzone

The repo root is also where the diagnostics and verification commands live:

pnpm diagnostics:illustrator
pnpm diagnostics:after-effects
pnpm exec vitest run
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit

items.title: CEP Panel Problems
items.text:
If the panel opens but does not see your Illustrator or After Effects document:

  • make sure the source file is saved
  • restart the host app after updating the panel
  • verify that the latest panel package is actually installed

If export fails from the panel, use the diagnostics commands from the repo root:

pnpm diagnostics:illustrator
pnpm diagnostics:after-effects

items.title: Illustrator
items.text:
Common failure modes:

  • unsaved document
  • CMYK document instead of RGB
  • bad font mapping
  • invalid special-layer content such as a broken video URL or empty HTML hook

items.title: After Effects
items.text:
Common failure modes:

  • unsaved .aep
  • wrong active comp
  • missing output template
  • overlay layers not prefixed correctly

items.title: Figma
items.text:
Common failure modes:

  • stale or missing plugin build
  • manifest imported without a fresh dist/
  • no selected top-level frames
  • equal-width responsive variants
  • invalid JSONC in advanced config

items.title: SVG Import
items.text:
Common warnings are usually about one of these:

  • text that could not stay live and was rasterized
  • grouping names that are ambiguous or invalid
  • unsupported effects preserved in the raster background
  • missing linked assets

If you are testing Canva exports, prefer ZIP or folder inputs with stable filenames and keep the responsive suffixes consistent.

items.title: How It Works
items.text: all2html has one central idea: every input surface should converge on the same intermediate format before rendering happens.

items.title: The Flow
items.text:
Design tool or importer
→ canonical IR
→ core pipeline
→ emitter
→ output files

That means Illustrator, After Effects, Figma, and SVG import all target the same downstream contract instead of carrying their own private HTML renderers.

items.title: Why The IR Matters
items.text:
The canonical IR is the boundary between extraction and rendering.

  • plugins/importers are responsible for understanding the source tool
  • the core pipeline is responsible for normalization, grouping, and rendering prep
  • emitters are responsible for writing HTML, Standalone HTML, Svelte, or React output

That keeps the output logic shared even when the source tools are very different.

items.title: Read More
items.text:
• Canonical IR
  • Pipeline
  • Responsive Output
  • Special Layers

items.title: Canonical IR
items.text: The IR is the contract between every input path and the shared rendering core.

items.title: Document
items.text:
The top-level record. It carries:

  • generator metadata
  • settings
  • fonts
  • artboards
  • assets
  • custom blocks
  • metadata
  • irVersion

items.title: Artboard
items.text: An artboard is the export unit that ultimately becomes a graphic variant in the output. It has dimensions, layers, and optional responsiveness/image-only flags.

items.title: Layer
items.text:
Layers control grouping and export behavior. A layer can be:

  • default content
  • PNG overlay
  • SVG overlay
  • inline SVG
  • video
  • raw HTML hook
  • snippet

items.title: Element
items.text:
Elements are the typed objects inside layers. The canonical element families are:

  • text
  • shape
  • video
  • raw HTML
  • snippet

Text elements carry paragraphs and runs so typography survives the trip out of the source tool whenever possible.

items.title: Shared Rules
items.text:
The IR uses a few important conventions:

  • canonical camelCase keys
  • absolute pixel positions
  • letterSpacing in em
  • opacity on a 0–100 scale in the base IR
  • renderAs: "html" | "image" on text elements when the exporter needs to explain whether text stays live

These rules matter because they let different tools feed the same pipeline without emitter-specific exceptions.

items.title: Versioning
items.text: Document.irVersion is required. Right now the repo uses "0.0.0" for pre-release evolution, but the field is already the forward/backward compatibility hook for future schema changes.

items.title: Pipeline
items.text: Once a tool has produced canonical IR, the same core pipeline takes over.

items.title: 1. Validate
items.text: The IR is checked against the shared schema. This is where malformed JSON, invalid enum values, or structural mismatches fail early.

items.title: 2. Resolve Settings
items.text: The pipeline turns partial settings into a full resolved settings object using canonical defaults plus any inline or external config.

items.title: 3. Group Artboards
items.text: Artboards are grouped into responsive sets when their names or input metadata indicate that they belong together.

items.title: 4. Compute Render-Ready Values
items.text:
This is where the core prepares the document for emitters:

  • breakpoints
  • responsive behavior
  • text/style normalization
  • asset path behavior
  • emitter-ready layer structure

items.title: 5. Emit
items.text:
Finally, an emitter writes output files:

  • HTML fragment
  • Standalone HTML
  • Svelte component
  • React component

The pipeline is shared so that importers and plugins do not each reinvent rendering.

items.title: Why This Split Is Useful
items.text:
It lets you:

  • add new input surfaces without rewriting emitters
  • add new emitters without touching source-tool extraction
  • inspect ir.json and debug failures at a stable boundary

items.title: Responsive Output
items.text: Responsiveness in all2html comes from grouping artboards or frames that represent the same story at different widths.

items.title: Fixed
items.text: Use fixed when the artboard should render at a defined width and swap to another artboard when a breakpoint is crossed.

items.title: Dynamic
items.text: Use dynamic when the layout itself should scale more fluidly instead of behaving like a locked-width panel.

items.title: Grouping
items.text:
Different input surfaces express grouping differently, but they all map to the same idea:

  • Illustrator: related artboards
  • Figma: selected frames with the same base name
  • SVG import: related files such as story--640.svg and story--960.svg

The pipeline then turns those into responsive groups that emitters can render consistently.

items.title: Image Handling
items.text: Responsive image handling also stays in the shared settings surface. That is why imported SVGs, Illustrator exports, and Figma exports can all feed the same HTML/CSS image behavior.

items.title: Failure Cases
items.text: The important rule is that grouping should be explicit and trustworthy. Equal-width variants in the same group fail instead of silently guessing.

items.title: Special Layers
items.text: Special layers are how all2html exports more than “background image plus text.”

items.title: Common Layer Types
items.text:
The current naming contract across the richer surfaces includes:

  • :png
  • :svg
  • :svg:inline
  • :video
  • :html-before
  • :html-after

Illustrator currently has the deepest support, but the naming model is shared where it makes sense.

items.title: Raster Background
items.text: Anything that should remain part of the flattened visual treatment ends up in the background image output.

items.title: Separate Overlay
items.text: PNG, SVG, and video layers can become independent overlays instead of being baked into the background.

items.title: HTML Hook
items.text: html-before and html-after let you inject controlled raw HTML around the artboard output.

items.title: Live Text Vs Image Text
items.text:
Text does not always stay live:

  • safe, mappable text can remain HTML
  • rotated, transformed, path, or explicitly image-only text can be rendered as image content instead

That tradeoff is recorded in the IR so the emitter does not need to guess.

items.title: After Effects
items.text: The After Effects path turns a comp into a video export plus timed HTML overlays. It is different from Illustrator on purpose: it is about temporal graphics, not responsive artboards.

items.text:
• After Effects script
  • Panel .zxp
  • Panel .zip
  • Install .zxp with ZXPInstaller

items.title: Packaged .jsx Script
items.text: This is the simplest path for AE users. Download all2html-after-effects.zip, unzip it, and run all2html-ae.jsx.

items.title: Shared Panel
items.text:
The panel (technically a CEP panel) adds an interface for:

  • comp selection
  • overlay prefix override
  • output-root override
  • output-module templates
  • font mapping
  • export diagnostics

items.title: Core Workflow
items.text:
1. Open and save the .aep file.
  2. Make the target comp active.
  3. Prefix overlay text layers with overlay:.
  4. Run the script or export from the panel.
  5. Collect the generated video, HTML, JSON, and summary files.

By default, output is written next to the project under all2html-ae-output/<comp-slug>/.

items.title: What Gets Exported
items.text:
The AE exporter is intentionally focused:

  • the rendered video
  • timed text overlays from matching layers
  • sampled layout/timing/style information needed to place the overlays

It is not trying to recreate every AE feature as editable web content.

items.title: Fonts And Project Config
items.text:
The standalone script and the panel both read project-local configuration from all2html-ae.config.json next to the .aep.

That file is used for:

  • font mappings
  • overlay prefix
  • output root
  • video template
  • poster template

items.title: Current Limits
items.text:
The AE exporter is useful now, but it is narrower than Illustrator:

  • one active comp at a time
  • no batch export
  • no responsive variants
  • no shape/SVG overlay export
  • text animation details are sampled values, not semantic reconstructions

That is expected. It is the right tool when you need HTML over rendered motion, not when you need an artboard-driven layout system.

Screenshot placeholder Crop the AE panel export section or a rendered output folder showing the video, HTML, and summary files together.

items.title: Figma
items.text: The Figma plugin works well now and fits the same pipeline as the other surfaces.

items.title: Download
items.text: • Figma plugin .zip

items.title: Install Shape
items.text:
1. Download all2html-figma-plugin.zip.
  2. Unzip it.
  3. In Figma, choose Import plugin from manifest...
  4. Select manifest.json.

The extracted folder needs to stay intact because the manifest points at built files inside dist/.

items.title: Core Workflow
items.text:
1. Open a Figma file.
  2. Select one or more top-level frames.
  3. Name frames with all2html-style annotations such as:
  4. story:640
  5. story:960
  6. story:dynamic
  7. story:image
  8. Run the imported all2html plugin.
  9. Choose a preset and output format.
  10. Export the ZIP bundle.

items.title: What The UI Exports Today
items.text:
The current plugin UI exports:

  • HTML
  • Standalone HTML

The plugin downloads a ZIP that includes:

  • ir.json
  • emitted output files
  • extracted assets

items.title: Frame Rules
items.text:
Figma follows a tighter selection contract than Illustrator:

  • only selected top-level frames export
  • frames with the same base name become a responsive group
  • equal-width variants in the same group fail clearly

This is deliberate. It makes the export surface explicit instead of guessing.

items.title: Config And Special Layers
items.text:
The plugin keeps shared config in figma.root plugin data and local convenience state in figma.clientStorage.

Top-level tagged child nodes inside a selected frame can define special layers with the Illustrator-aligned naming contract:

  • :png
  • :svg
  • :svg:inline
  • :video
  • :html-before
  • :html-after

items.title: What Figma Is Good For Right Now
items.text:
• newsroom story frames
  • responsive frame groups
  • direct export from a UI instead of handwritten JSON
  • special hooks and visual overlays

It is less about full-file auto-discovery and more about clean, selected export roots.

Screenshot placeholder Crop the Figma plugin UI showing the selection summary, preset selector, and export format controls.

items.text: Illustrator is the center of gravity for all2html. If you want the most ai2html-like path, this is it.

items.title: Script
items.text:
Use the script when you want the original File → Scripts workflow and document-local settings through ai2html-settings.

Open Illustrator, select File > Scripts > Other Scripts... from the top menu and browse to the .js file.

items.title: The Panel
items.text:
The panel is much more fun! Use the panel – technically a CEP panel – when you want:

  • app defaults
  • per-document settings UI
  • font mapping UI
  • diagnostics
  • Open folder

The panel is the better install for people who use all2html frequently.

items.title: Core Workflow
items.text:
1. Open a saved Illustrator document.
  2. Create one or more artboards.
  3. Add text, overlays, and special layers.
  4. Run the script or export from the panel.
  5. Rejoice in the the generated HTML/images.

Output is written next to the document by default in all2html-output/.

items.title: Important Settings
items.text:
Illustrator supports much of the classic ai2html-style setting surface. The highest-visibility settings are:

  • image_format
  • responsiveness
  • output
  • html_output_path
  • image_output_path
  • jpg_quality
  • png_number_of_colors
  • use_2x_images_if_possible

You can set them in:

  • an ai2html-settings text block in the document
  • all2html.config.json next to the document
  • the CEP panel

The panel also shows where values are coming from and lets you save defaults.

items.title: Special Layers
items.text:
Illustrator supports the richest set of special layers today. The main ones are:

  • :png
  • :svg
  • :svg:inline
  • :video
  • :html-before
  • :html-after
  • :symbol
  • :div

These either stay as overlays/hooks or influence how the final background and HTML are built. They are explained in more detail in Special Layers.

items.title: Fonts
items.text:
Font mapping is done through all2html.config.json or the panel UI. The common case is mapping an Illustrator font name to a web family and weight:

{
  "fonts": [
    {
      "aifont": "HelveticaNeue-Bold",
      "family": "'Helvetica Neue', sans-serif",
      "weight": "700"
    }
  ]
}

items.title: What Illustrator Is Best For
items.text:
• artboard-based responsive graphics
  • classic newsroom ai2html workflows
  • special-layer overlays and hooks
  • deterministic background image generation

Screenshot placeholder Crop the main panel settings area plus one visible badge or font-mapping row.

items.title: SVG Conversion
items.text: The SVG importer is the tool-agnostic path. It is especially useful for Canva exports, but it is not Canva-specific in the architecture.

items.title: Open It
items.text: • Open the SVG browser converter

items.title: Inputs It Accepts
items.text:
You can import:

  • one SVG file
  • a folder of SVG files
  • a ZIP of SVG files

The browser app and the CLI both feed the same core importer and pipeline.

items.title: Why This Matters For Canva
items.text: Canva’s multi-page SVG export becomes a set of per-page SVGs, often packaged as a ZIP. all2html can treat those files as artboards and run them through the same HTML pipeline as every other surface.

items.title: CLI
items.text:
all2html import svg export.zip -o output/
all2html import svg export.zip -o output/ --format standalone
all2html import svg export.zip -o output/ --format svelte

items.title: Browser App
items.text:
Public page: svg-converter

pnpm dev:svg-dropzone
pnpm build:svg-dropzone

The browser app is fully client-side and accepts drag-and-drop SVG or ZIP input.

items.title: Naming Rules
items.text:
Responsive grouping is driven by filenames. Preferred examples:

  • story--640.svg
  • story--960.svg
  • story--dynamic.svg
  • story--image.svg

Colon-style names such as story:640 are still accepted where that convention already exists.

items.title: Live Text And Raster Backgrounds
items.text:
The importer tries to recover live HTML text when the SVG text can be mapped safely. The rest of the SVG is rasterized into ai2html-style PNG or JPG backgrounds by default.

That means:

  • text can stay editable/live when possible
  • complex vector effects can still render correctly as background imagery
  • --image naming or image-only settings can force a fully rasterized result

items.title: Formats
items.text:
The SVG importer supports the full emitter surface:

  • HTML
  • Standalone HTML
  • Svelte
  • React

items.title: Good Uses
items.text:
• Canva export translation
  • generic SVG-to-web conversion
  • multi-file responsive graphics
  • one-off visual tests through the browser app

items.title: Formats
items.text: all2html currently emits four main web output targets.

items.title: HTML
items.text: The standard fragment output. Use this when the result will be embedded into a larger page or CMS surface.

items.title: Standalone HTML
items.text: A self-contained page wrapper around the same rendered content. Use this when you want something easy to open directly in a browser or hand to someone as a complete page.

items.title: Svelte
items.text: A component-oriented output for teams that want to integrate the result into a Svelte application.

items.title: React
items.text: A component-oriented output for teams that want to integrate the result into a React application.

items.title: Common Bundle Shape
items.text:
Most export surfaces also involve:

  • ir.json
  • raster backgrounds or extracted assets
  • emitted output files

That bundle shape is what makes the examples gallery and source/output samples practical.

items.title: IR Schema
items.text: This is the public technical summary of the canonical IR. It is intentionally descriptive rather than a raw dump of TypeScript or Zod source.

items.title: Top-Level Shape
items.text:
A document includes:

  • generator
  • settings
  • fonts
  • artboards
  • assets
  • customBlocks
  • metadata
  • irVersion

items.title: Generator
items.text: Tracks which tool or importer created the IR and which versions were involved.

items.title: Fonts
items.text: Font mappings normalize source-tool font names into web-ready family/weight/style information.

items.title: Artboards
items.text:
Each artboard contains:

  • dimensions
  • name/original name
  • optional responsiveness metadata
  • layers

items.title: Layers And Elements
items.text: Layers contain typed elements. Text is carried as paragraphs and runs so emitters can preserve actual typography rather than treating everything as one string.

items.title: Assets
items.text: Assets are exported files such as background images or overlay files. The asset key and the asset id must match.

items.title: Metadata
items.text: Metadata carries document-level information like slug, alt text, and language. Accessibility information belongs here, not in random tool-specific side channels.

items.title: Key Validation Rules
items.text:
• irVersion is required
  • Paragraph.text must match the concatenation of its runs
  • asset IDs and asset map keys must agree
  • unit conventions are fixed so emitters can trust them

items.title: Units
items.text:
• positions: pixels
  • fontSize, leading, spaceBefore, spaceAfter: pixels
  • letterSpacing: em
  • opacity in base IR: 0–100

items.title: Settings Reference
items.text: all2html keeps one canonical settings model even though each source tool exposes it differently.

items.title: Output
items.text:
• output
  • htmlOutputPath
  • imageOutputPath
  • slug

items.title: Responsiveness
items.text:
• responsiveness
  • textResponsiveness
  • responsiveImageMode

items.title: Images
items.text:
• imageFormat
  • jpgQuality
  • pngNumberOfColors
  • use2xImages

items.title: HTML Behavior
items.text:
• namespace
  • clickableLink
  • inlineSvg

items.title: Accessibility And Metadata
items.text:
These mostly live in metadata rather than settings:

  • altText
  • imageAltText
  • ariaRole
  • lang

items.title: Canonical Naming
items.text: Inside the IR and core config parsing, settings always use canonical camelCase keys. Tool-native snake_case belongs only on the tool side of the boundary.

items.title: Where Settings Come From
items.text:
Depending on the surface, settings can come from:

  • document annotations
  • config files
  • panel UI state
  • plugin UI controls
  • CLI config

The important point is that they all resolve to the same final settings object before emitting output.
